title: React Native & TypeScript Interviews
description: Type-safe mobile UI, React reasoning, native behavior, performance, and reliable app workflows.

courses.title: React Native & TypeScript Interviews
courses.description: Type-safe mobile UI, React reasoning, native behavior, performance, and reliable app workflows.

chapters.title: 1 · TypeScript for mobile apps
chapters.summary: Turn uncertain API input into explicit and safe UI states.

lessons.title: Unions and runtime boundaries
lessons.explanation: Use types to encode states without trusting network data blindly.

exercises.prompt: fetch returns an untrusted JSON payload. Which type should represent it before validation?
options: any and an unchecked cast to User
User because the endpoint says so
never because JSON may be absent
exercises.explanation: A TypeScript type does not validate runtime JSON; unknown forces a check before domain use.

exercises.prompt: A request can load, succeed with rows, or fail with an error. Which type forbids a success state with an error?
options: An object with optional rows and optional error
A discriminated union with separate status cases
exercises.explanation: Each union variant carries only its valid data, and status narrows the branch.

exercises.prompt: A new screen state is added but a switch omits it. What reveals the omission at compile time?
options: An any cast on the state
An exhaustive default assigning the remaining value to never
A default that returns null for everything
exercises.explanation: A never check fails when a new variant remains after known cases.

exercises.prompt: A repository wrapper should return the precise parsed model type. What does a generic function preserve?
options: The relationship between validated input and output model type
exercises.explanation: Generics retain compile-time relationships; the parser still must validate runtime data.

exercises.prompt: An API distinguishes an omitted patch field from an explicit null that clears it. Which property type can express both?
exercises.explanation: The optional marker permits absence; the null union permits an explicit clear operation.

exercises.prompt: A function receives Readonly<User> where User has tags: string[]. What is still possible?
options: Changing every field through TypeScript reflection only
Mutating the nested tags array through a reference
exercises.explanation: Readonly is shallow at the type level; use deep immutable modeling where nested mutation must be prevented.

exercises.prompt: A TypeScript union says status is active or inactive, but JSON contains pending. What should the app do?
options: Reject or explicitly map the unknown value at the boundary
Assume the type union converted it
exercises.explanation: Static types do not alter incoming bytes; runtime decoding must handle unsupported values.

exercises.prompt: Fill the safe type for raw response data before parsing.
exercises.template:
const payload: ____1 = await response.json();
const user = parseUser(payload);
exercises.explanation: unknown requires the parser to prove the shape before the app treats it as User.

lessons.title: Precise app contracts
lessons.explanation: Choose types that maintain caller and state relationships.

exercises.prompt: A helper reads a known property from a model. Which key constraint rejects misspelled property names?
exercises.explanation: keyof T restricts keys to properties of T and keeps the return type T[K].

exercises.prompt: A profile patch accepts only supplied fields. What risk comes from applying Partial<Profile> directly to domain state?
options: It does not validate runtime input or distinguish every clear semantics automatically
It removes every property from Profile
It forces all fields to null
exercises.explanation: Partial is a compile-time convenience; API patch rules and runtime validation still need explicit handling.

exercises.prompt: A UI preview should receive a User except passwordHash. Which utility type models that compile-time omission?
exercises.explanation: Omit excludes the sensitive property from the view-facing type. Actual serialization must also omit it.

exercises.prompt: A reducer handles add, remove, and reset with different payloads. Which event shape narrows safely?
options: A string and an unrelated global variable
A number enum with arbitrary data
A union keyed by literal type fields with case-specific payloads
One object with optional payload: any
exercises.explanation: A discriminant connects each action to its required payload.

exercises.prompt: A catch variable is unknown. What is the safe way to show a message?
options: Treat it as a string always
Narrow with instanceof Error and provide a fallback for other throws
exercises.explanation: JavaScript can throw any value, so a user-facing message requires narrowing.

exercises.prompt: Both UserID and OrderID are strings and are accidentally mixed. Which type-level design can catch this?
options: Distinct branded ID types at domain boundaries
Using number for one arbitrary endpoint
exercises.explanation: Brands can prevent accidental cross-domain string substitution at compile time, though runtime values still need validation.

exercises.prompt: A developer writes response as Profile after JSON parsing. What does that assertion do at runtime?
options: Nothing; it only tells the compiler to trust the developer
exercises.explanation: Type assertions do not emit runtime checks and can hide malformed payloads.

exercises.prompt: Fill the type used to reveal an unhandled discriminated-union variant.
exercises.template: default: { const missing: ____1 = state; return missing; }
exercises.explanation: If every variant was handled, the remaining state type is never.

chapters.title: 2 · React reasoning
chapters.summary: Avoid stale state, effect races, and identity bugs.

lessons.title: State and closures
lessons.explanation: Trace React updates using the state snapshot model.

exercises.prompt: Two rapid presses each increment a counter from the same render. Which updater preserves both increments?
exercises.explanation: The functional updater receives the latest queued state; a captured count can be stale.

exercises.prompt: An interval callback always logs count = 0 after count changes. What is the likely cause?
options: Intervals always run on a native thread
setCount mutates the variable in place
The callback closed over the count from the initial render
exercises.explanation: Closures capture render snapshots. Update dependencies or use a ref/function updater for the intended behavior.

exercises.prompt: An effect fetches by userId but has an empty dependency array. What happens when userId changes?
options: The request is canceled by TypeScript
The effect does not rerun for the new ID
React automatically inspects the fetch URL
exercises.explanation: Dependencies specify which reactive values should restart the effect.

exercises.prompt: A screen subscribes to AppState in an effect. What should cleanup do?
options: Remove that subscription when the effect ends
exercises.explanation: Cleanup prevents duplicate listeners and work after the component lifetime.

exercises.prompt: Messages reorder and each row has local draft state. What key maintains correct row identity?
options: The message text if duplicate texts exist
exercises.explanation: Stable keys attach local state to the same item across reorders.

exercises.prompt: A derived array is cheap to compute. Should useMemo be added automatically?
options: Yes; memoizing all values is always free
No; React Native cannot use useMemo
No; measure render cost and dependency behavior first
exercises.explanation: Memoization adds complexity and has its own cost; use it for measured work or referential stability needs.

exercises.prompt: A large context value object is recreated each render and many consumers update. What is a focused improvement?
options: Store context in a global mutable object
Split state by concern or stabilize provider value when profiling shows a cost
Wrap every screen in a new provider
exercises.explanation: Context consumers respond to value identity changes; smaller scopes reduce unrelated work.

exercises.prompt: Fill the update that uses the latest queued state after repeated taps.
exercises.explanation: A functional updater avoids reading a stale render snapshot.

lessons.title: Effects and reconciliation
lessons.explanation: Make request lifetime and render purity explicit.

exercises.prompt: Complete a latest-request-wins search handler.
exercises.hiddenTests: Search A then B, resolve B then A: only B rows remain visible.

guided.explanation: Each request gets a generation. Apply its rows only if no later request has replaced it.

exercises.explanation: Each request gets a generation. Apply its rows only if no later request has replaced it.

exercises.prompt: A component starts a network request in its render body. Why is that unsafe?
options: It automatically blocks all other screens
Rendering can repeat without committing, causing duplicate work
Network calls are forbidden by TypeScript
exercises.explanation: Rendering should describe UI; effects belong to a managed lifecycle boundary.

exercises.prompt: A filtered array is wholly determined by items and query. What is the simplest state model?
options: Derive it during render, memoizing only if needed
Store a second independent filtered state that can drift
Keep filtered rows in a global variable
exercises.explanation: Duplicating derived state creates synchronization bugs; compute from sources of truth.

exercises.prompt: A form should intentionally reset when accountId changes. Which identity tool can do that?
options: Use an array index as key
Keep all fields in a module global
exercises.explanation: Changing key creates a new component identity and resets its local state deliberately.

exercises.prompt: A mutable request ID must be read by callbacks but should not trigger rendering. Where should it live?
options: A new local variable in render
A prop mutated by the child
exercises.explanation: A ref persists across renders without scheduling a render when changed.

exercises.prompt: An effect depends on an inline object created every render, then sets state. Why can it loop?
options: The JS engine changes hook order randomly
The object identity changes each render, retriggering the effect
useEffect never reruns after state updates
exercises.explanation: Dependencies compare by identity for objects. Move stable inputs into the dependency list or memoize deliberately.

exercises.prompt: A checkout has idle, pending, confirmed, and failed transitions. When is a reducer especially useful?
options: When related transitions need one explicit state machine
When every state is a Boolean
Only when a native module is used
exercises.explanation: A reducer centralizes transition logic and helps prevent impossible combinations.

exercises.prompt: Fill the cleanup that prevents a late request from committing after selection changes.
exercises.template: useEffect(() => { let active = true; load(id).then(v => { if (active) setData(v); }); return () => { ____1; }; }, [id]);
exercises.explanation: Cleanup marks this effect instance stale before its result callback can apply.

chapters.title: 3 · React Native UI
chapters.summary: Handle long lists, layout, gestures, keyboard, and accessibility.

lessons.title: Lists and layout
lessons.explanation: Apply native mobile layout constraints and identity.

exercises.prompt: A feed contains thousands of rows. Which component should render it lazily?
exercises.explanation: FlatList virtualizes rows; ScrollView renders all children up front.

exercises.prompt: Rows reorder after a server refresh. What should keyExtractor return?
options: A stable item ID from the server
exercises.explanation: Stable keys preserve row identity through insertion and reorder.

exercises.prompt: A row unexpectedly stacks children vertically in React Native. What style usually changes direction?
exercises.explanation: React Native Flexbox defaults to column; row lays children horizontally.

exercises.prompt: A long title overflows beside a fixed icon in a row. What often gives the text bounded remaining space?
options: A text wrapper with flexShrink: 1 or appropriate flex sizing
exercises.explanation: Text needs a constraint in the row to wrap or truncate; web CSS properties do not apply directly.

exercises.prompt: A bottom action overlaps gesture navigation on some Android devices. Which layout input should the screen respect?
options: Safe-area insets and current edge-to-edge configuration
exercises.explanation: System inset sizes vary by device and navigation mode; the action should clear the system gesture region.

exercises.prompt: A remote image flickers and shifts nearby content when loaded. What should be reserved before fetch completes?
options: Known width and height or an aspectRatio constraint
exercises.explanation: Reserving dimensions prevents layout jump when image data arrives.

exercises.prompt: onLayout sets state on every pass to a slightly different value. What is a likely symptom?
options: Repeated layout/render work or a feedback loop
exercises.explanation: State updates trigger rendering and potentially another layout; update only when a meaningful value changes.

exercises.prompt: Fill the item identity source for a virtualized list.
exercises.explanation: Stable domain IDs preserve row identity after inserts and reorders.

lessons.title: Interaction and accessibility
lessons.explanation: Account for keyboard, Back, and touch semantics.

exercises.prompt: A focused input is covered by the keyboard on a short screen. What should the layout address?
options: Keyboard-aware resizing or scrolling with safe-area spacing
A forced full-screen modal for every input
exercises.explanation: The focused field must remain visible when the keyboard changes usable height.

exercises.prompt: A heart icon button has no text. What should it expose to a screen reader?
options: An accessibility label and button role describing the action
The file name of its SVG
exercises.explanation: Assistive technology needs the action meaning, not just visual shape.

exercises.prompt: A 16-pixel icon is hard to tap. Which change improves it without enlarging the drawing?
options: Increase the pressable area with padding or hitSlop
exercises.explanation: A larger touch target improves usability while artwork can remain small.

exercises.prompt: Android Back is pressed inside a lesson with unsaved selections. What should navigation decide?
options: Whether to abandon or preserve the lesson run, then navigate consistently
exercises.explanation: Back navigation should follow the same progress rule as leaving via an on-screen control.

exercises.prompt: A horizontal swipe card sits inside a vertical list. What must gesture design account for?
options: Direction thresholds and responder coordination so scrolling still works
Always capture every touch for the card
exercises.explanation: Competing gestures need a clear activation policy on native touch systems.

exercises.prompt: A behavior differs between Android and iOS. Where should that difference be expressed?
options: At a small platform boundary or platform-specific component
In a global mutable flag scattered through the app
exercises.explanation: Narrow platform boundaries keep shared behavior readable and testable.

exercises.prompt: A row reads its price before its product name in accessibility focus despite visual order. What should be reviewed?
options: The accessible grouping and traversal order of its native elements
exercises.explanation: Visual placement does not guarantee useful spoken order; grouping and labels should convey the row meaning.

exercises.prompt: Fill the role for a pressable icon that adds an item.
exercises.explanation: A pressable action should announce itself as a button.

chapters.title: 4 · Architecture and performance
chapters.summary: Control data ownership, renders, and native boundaries.

lessons.title: State and cache
lessons.explanation: Keep server data and local edits consistent.

exercises.prompt: A screen should show cached rows offline and refresh online. What should UI observe?
options: A local repository snapshot updated by validated network writes
A fetch in every row render
exercises.explanation: A local source of truth supports offline display and coherent updates.

exercises.prompt: Two product screens use the same cache entry despite different IDs. What is likely wrong?
exercises.explanation: Request identity must include every parameter that changes the result.

exercises.prompt: A like action updates immediately, then the server rejects it. What should the client do?
options: Retry with a new action ID forever
Rollback or reconcile that operation and show useful feedback
exercises.explanation: Optimistic state needs a failure path linked to the same mutation.

exercises.prompt: Rows rerender frequently despite unchanged row data. What should be measured first?
options: The number of comments in source
Which props and callbacks change identity and whether rerenders are costly
exercises.explanation: Profiling reveals whether referential changes or expensive row work matter before adding memoization.

exercises.prompt: A device API is unavailable in JavaScript. What should a native module expose?
options: A narrow async method or event contract with typed inputs and errors
The entire Android Activity object to JS
A raw pointer kept in React state
exercises.explanation: A small explicit boundary limits platform coupling and makes error handling testable.

exercises.prompt: A high-frequency sensor sends large arrays to JS every frame. What is a likely bottleneck even with modern native interop?
options: The number of lessons in JSON
Cross-boundary serialization and JS/render work at that frequency
exercises.explanation: Reduce, batch, or sample data at the native boundary rather than flooding JS with every raw event.

exercises.prompt: Typing in one search input rerenders a whole dashboard. What state placement might improve this?
options: Keep transient query state near the search feature and profile consumers
Move query into one global context containing all dashboard data
exercises.explanation: Localizing fast-changing state limits unrelated subscribers.

exercises.prompt: Fill the key component needed to separate cached item details.
exercises.explanation: A stable ID makes cache identity follow the requested product.

lessons.title: Diagnostics and testing
lessons.explanation: Verify behavior at the right boundaries.

exercises.prompt: Debug works but minified Android release crashes before JS starts. What should be inspected first?
options: Native release logs and shrinker rules for reflected classes
exercises.explanation: Release shrinking can remove classes used reflectively; Logcat shows native startup failures.

exercises.prompt: A screen test should verify canceling an old search. What behavior matters?
options: Old A results never replace newer B results after both resolve
The hook has a particular variable name
A live production API is called
exercises.explanation: The test should control response order and assert visible state, not internal naming.

exercises.prompt: A native package is installed but the running development build lacks its module. What is required?
options: Rebuild the native app after adding the native dependency
exercises.explanation: Metro can refresh JS, but a newly linked native module must be compiled into the binary.

exercises.prompt: A navigation screen leaks after it is popped. Which resources should be checked?
options: AppState listeners, timers, subscriptions, and retained closures
exercises.explanation: Long-lived listeners and callbacks can retain screen state after unmount unless cleaned up.

exercises.prompt: What is a meaningful offline smoke test for a saved lesson?
options: Force-stop, disable network, relaunch, and verify progress and questions remain available
Only load the screen once with Metro running
Check JSON syntax without opening the app
exercises.explanation: Restart plus offline use proves the local source of truth is actually durable and bundled content loads.

exercises.prompt: A long list stalls during scroll. Which evidence distinguishes JS render work from native image decode cost?
options: A device profile or trace covering JS and UI frame timing
A guess based on file names
exercises.explanation: Frame traces point to the actual bottleneck; optimization should follow measured work.

exercises.prompt: An interviewer asks whether the new architecture eliminates all cross-language costs. What is accurate?
options: It makes every native call free
It removes the need for native builds
It changes interop mechanisms, but boundary volume and JS/UI work still matter
exercises.explanation: Architecture improvements do not make high-frequency large payload transfers or rendering work costless.

exercises.prompt: Fill the cleanup for an AppState subscription owned by an effect.
exercises.template: useEffect(() => { const sub = AppState.addEventListener("change", onState); return () => sub.____1(); }, []);
exercises.explanation: Removing the subscription prevents duplicate callbacks and retained screen closures.

chapters.title: 5 · Production mobile workflows
chapters.summary: Handle auth, offline edits, notifications, and uncertain outcomes.

lessons.title: Requests and lifecycle
lessons.explanation: Make network work safe as screens and app state change.

exercises.prompt: An app must persist an auth refresh token. Where should it go?
options: Platform secure storage with an appropriate accessibility policy
A source constant committed to Git
exercises.explanation: Tokens belong in OS-backed secure storage, separate from portable learner progress.

exercises.prompt: Five requests get 401 and all refresh a token at once. What avoids conflicting refreshes?
options: Retry each request with the expired token
A single-flight refresh operation shared by pending requests
exercises.explanation: Coalescing refresh work preserves one new credential and lets requests resume consistently.

exercises.prompt: A screen leaves while its fetch is pending. What should the request owner do?
options: Abort when possible and prevent late state application
exercises.explanation: Cancellation and stale guards align request lifetime with the screen or repository owner.

exercises.prompt: A user edits a profile offline. What must be persisted to resume sync after process death?
options: The edit payload, stable operation ID, and pending status
exercises.explanation: A durable command lets the app retry the same logical edit after restart.

exercises.prompt: A push notification targets order 42 while the app is cold. What should navigation use?
options: Parse and validate a stable order ID, then load the order
A live component reference serialized in the push
Assume the order is in memory
exercises.explanation: Cold starts need restorable route data and loading or missing states.

exercises.prompt: The app resumes from background. What is a safe refresh behavior?
options: Run refresh in every row render
Assume background work never changes data
Refresh according to staleness policy while preserving cached content
exercises.explanation: A resume refresh should not erase usable offline state while networking is uncertain.

exercises.prompt: A payment POST times out. What can the client conclude?
options: A new random ID makes retry safe
The result is uncertain until reconciled by stable operation ID
exercises.explanation: The server may have committed before the response was lost; idempotency and reconciliation matter.

exercises.prompt: Fill the object passed to fetch so an effect cleanup can cancel it.
exercises.template:
const controller = new AbortController();
fetch(url, { signal: ____1 });
exercises.explanation: fetch accepts an AbortSignal; cleanup can call controller.abort().

lessons.title: Reliable state transitions
lessons.explanation: Preserve causality across retries and app restarts.

exercises.prompt: A local offline edit and a server edit both change the same field. What does sync need?
options: A documented conflict rule with versions or domain merge semantics
Always trust whichever response arrives last
Always drop the local edit without telling the user
exercises.explanation: Arrival order is not user intent; revisions reveal concurrent changes.

exercises.prompt: An optimistic comment is retried and appears twice after server response. What would prevent this?
options: Match the server receipt to the stable client operation ID and merge by item ID
Generate a new temporary ID on each retry
exercises.explanation: Stable operation and item identity lets the client reconcile the optimistic row instead of duplicating it.

exercises.prompt: A local queue record and optimistic UI record must commit together. What protects against half-completion?
exercises.explanation: An atomic transaction keeps related local records consistent across crashes.

exercises.prompt: The same notification is delivered through foreground and open handlers. What prevents duplicate navigation?
options: Track a stable notification/action ID for the navigation event
exercises.explanation: Delivery paths can overlap; a stable event ID allows a one-time transition.

exercises.prompt: Many clients retry after an outage. Which policy lowers synchronized load?
options: Bounded exponential backoff with jitter for safe-to-retry operations
exercises.explanation: Jitter spreads clients; bounds control cost and idempotency determines whether a request can repeat.

exercises.prompt: A learner exports a progress backup. What must be excluded?
options: Purchase entitlement flags, credentials, and advertising IDs
exercises.explanation: Progress is portable; sensitive credentials and store entitlement state must remain with their verified owners.

exercises.prompt: Fill the ID reused on every attempt of one queued mutation.
exercises.explanation: One logical operation keeps one idempotency key across retries.

exercises.prompt: Repair a mobile offline mutation queue
exercises.story: A comment is submitted offline. The app can restart, and an HTTP timeout may happen after server commit. Complete the two stages.

parts.prompt: Settle confirmed results and retain uncertain commands.
parts.hiddenTests: A confirmed receipt completes once; an uncertain response remains pending for same-key retry.

guided.explanation: Send with the stable key, complete only confirmed work, and retry uncertain outcomes.
